title: Care Coordination Q&A: CGM Use and the Size of a Courtesy Reship Bridge
content:
A courtesy reship on the Blood Glucose Testing Supply Program reads the status of the customer's Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program and its recent sensor refills.

**Rule.** The strips a courtesy reship carries for its covered days and its transit days are multiplied by the sensor share, which is 0.6 when the customer's CGM program is active and a sensor refill shipped to the customer on any of the customer's CGM programs within the last 3 calendar months, because confirmation testing is all that the bridge must carry; 1.25 when the customer's CGM program is on hold; and 1 otherwise.

**Q. Is an active CGM program alone enough for 0.6?** No; a sensor refill shipped within the last 3 calendar months is also needed — its ship date later than the same calendar day 3 months earlier. Without one, an active CGM program leaves the share at 1.

**Q. Why does a hold raise the share?** While the CGM program is on hold the reship carries more fingerstick testing: 1.25.

**Q. Closed, referral received or pending authorization?** None of these is active or on hold, so the share is 1.

**Q. Boundary of the 3 months? (hypothetical: today is 30 April)** A sensor refill shipped 31 January falls within; one shipped 30 January does not.

**Worked figures.** Strips for the covered and transit days of 50.0 become 30.0 at 0.6 and 62.5 at 1.25.
